title: INT8 matmul kernel selection + correctness fallbacks (shape constraints, per-GPU support)
creator: Hiro Tanaka
description:
Implement INT8 matmul integration for the serving runtime with robust selection rules and correctness fallbacks.

This ticket is specifically about:
- When we select INT8 matmul vs baseline (BF16/FP16) per GPU SKU and shape regime.
- Guardrails to avoid known-bad shapes (alignment/stride/layout constraints, small-K regimes, odd batch/sequence tiling).
- Correctness fallback behavior (automatic revert to baseline kernels) with explicit observability signals.
- Unit tests that cover supported/unsupported shapes and validate fallback triggers.

Sprint context: FP8/INT8 kernel benchmarking sprint. INT8 matmul is a major contributor to prefill wins for several hosted models, but correctness and variance issues were observed in early harness runs when shapes were not aligned or when driver/CUDA differed across clusters. We need selection logic that is defensible, easy to reason about, and safe to roll out behind flags/perf canary.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Selection rules: Runtime only chooses INT8 matmul on supported GPUs and supported shapes; otherwise it must fall back to baseline automatically.
2) Supported GPU matrix is encoded explicitly (not inferred) and is queryable in logs/metrics.
3) Shape constraints are enforced in dispatch (k alignment / leading dimension / layout), with a single place to reason about them (no scattered checks).
4) Correctness fallback: if INT8 path hits unsupported shape or fails runtime validation, fallback occurs within the same request without crashing.
5) Unit tests: Must include (a) positive tests for supported shapes, (b) negative tests for unsupported shapes that assert baseline selection, and (c) at least one randomized coverage test per supported GPU family.
6) Observability: Metrics/logging tags include kernel_mode=int8|baseline and a reason code when falling back (e.g., fallback_reason=shape_guard|gpu_unsupported|validation_failed).
7) Documentation: Internal notes (docstring / runtime config comments) describing constraints and how to add new shapes/SKUs.
implementation_notes:
Proposed dispatch contract (high level):
- Input: (GPU arch/SKU, dtype policy, model config: hidden size, intermediate size, group size if applicable, layout, runtime shape: M/N/K).
- Output: kernel implementation ID (int8_matmul_vX | baseline_matmul_vY) + fallback_reason if not selecting INT8.

Per-GPU support (initial):
- H100 (SM90): supported (primary target)
- A100 (SM80): supported with stricter guards; expected smaller win vs H100
- L4 (Ada): not enabled by default during sprint; allow explicit opt-in flag for experiments only

Shape/layout guardrails (initial; can be relaxed later with evidence):
- K must be a multiple of 16 (hard fail -> baseline)
- N must be a multiple of 8 (hard fail -> baseline)
- For A100: prefer K multiple of 32; otherwise baseline (avoid noisy perf and occasional correctness anomalies seen in early runs)
- Enforce contiguous/expected layout for weight matrix (baseline if non-standard strides)
- Disallow very small M (micro-batches) where launch overhead dominates unless benchmarked (baseline for M < threshold)

Correctness strategy:
- Always keep baseline path available.
- If INT8 kernel returns error code / unexpected status, immediately fallback to baseline for that op and increment fallback counter.
- Add a lightweight validation toggle for debug builds / CI runs (compare INT8 vs baseline on a tiny subset of ops within tolerance). Default OFF in prod.

Owner note: This ticket intentionally does NOT decide global policy for FP8 vs INT8 for full model execution. It only makes matmul selection safe and testable; higher-level heuristics are tracked in ENG-7430 / ADR-019.
test_plan:
Unit tests (required):
- Dispatch tests (CPU-only): table-driven tests that feed in (gpu_arch, M/N/K, layout flags) and assert selected kernel ID and fallback_reason.
- Kernel correctness tests (GPU required):
  - H100: run a small suite of representative (M,N,K) shapes from top hosted models (prefill-heavy) and compare INT8 output to baseline BF16 within tolerance; include at least one awkward-but-supported shape.
  - A100: same, but with the stricter K-multiple-of-32 guard.
- Negative tests:
  - Non-aligned K and/or N -> assert baseline selection (no attempt to run INT8 kernel).
  - Non-contiguous weight layout -> baseline selection.

CI expectations:
- Add a smoke suite that runs on at least one GPU runner (H100 preferred; A100 acceptable) with a small set of shapes (<2 minutes).
- Tests must print the selected kernel_mode and fallback_reason to make triage easy when CI flakes.

Perf sanity:
- Not a perf benchmark ticket, but include one microbench assertion in nightly (tokens/s or matmul latency) to ensure we don’t accidentally route everything to baseline after refactors.
rollout_plan:
1) Land behind flag: runtime.int8_matmul.enabled (default OFF).
2) Enable in benchmark harness runs first (owned by Rina/Isabella) to confirm selection and artifact tagging.
3) Perf canary: enable for 1-2 models in one region cohort on H100 only; monitor TTFT/TPOT + error_rate + fallback_rate.
4) Expand to A100 after confirming fallback rate and correctness; keep stricter shape guards until we have stable evidence.
5) If fallback_rate spikes or quality/correctness issues appear, rollback by flag and open follow-up to refine constraints.

Rollback triggers:
- Any correctness failure signal (validation failure in canary builds) OR increased error rate.
- TTFT p95 regression above perf-canary thresholds for the canary cohort.
- Sustained fallback_rate > 5% (indicates guard mismatch with production shapes or layout assumptions).

comments: 2026-02-10 (Hiro Tanaka): We need the INT8 matmul path to be safe-by-default. Please bias toward explicit guards and a clear fallback reason code. We can relax later with data.

2026-02-11 (Grace Kim): Drafted initial constraints: K%16==0, N%8==0, contiguous weight layout only. Adding stricter A100 rule (K%32==0) based on early variance and one correctness failure in bench-lab.

2026-02-12 (Noah Patel): +1 on explicit fallback_reason. Please also tag metrics with kernel_mode and gpu_sku so canary triage can isolate quickly. We’ve been burned by silent fallbacks looking like perf regressions.

2026-02-14 (Isabella Rossi): Microbench shows INT8 wins disappear for tiny M (micro-batch). Suggest defaulting to baseline when M < 64 until we measure more; otherwise you see worse TTFT due to launch overhead.
2026-02-15 (Grace Kim): Implemented M-threshold guard (baseline when M < 64). Added dispatch unit tests for edge cases. Working on GPU correctness tests next; need H100 runner time.
2026-02-16 (Irene Choi): FYI H100 capacity window is 02/17-02/19 in us-east and 02/19-02/20 in eu-west. Please keep test suite short so we don’t collide with matrix runner jobs.

2026-02-17 (Grace Kim): GPU correctness suite passing on H100 (small shape set). A100 run showed one failure when K%32!=0; keeping A100 stricter guard for now and filing follow-up to investigate (likely alignment assumption).
2026-02-18 (Jonas Weber): For quality/evals, we don’t need INT8-by-default yet, but we do need rock-solid fallback so we can run perf experiments without worrying about silent correctness drift.
2026-02-20 (Grace Kim): PR up with dispatch + guards + tests. Added metric tag kernel_mode and fallback_reason. Please review the guard thresholds; they’re conservative but reflect current evidence.
2026-02-22 (Hiro Tanaka): Review: Looks good. Requested one more negative test to ensure non-contiguous weights always route to baseline, and a doc comment on how to add new GPU SKUs safely.
2026-02-23 (Grace Kim): Addressed review feedback. Added non-contig layout test + inline docs. Ready to merge.
2026-02-26 (Connor O'Brien): Marking done; landed in runtime-1.22 RC. Flag remains OFF by default pending perf canary signoff (ENG-7426).
